subject: general
question: The poultry birds grown for the purpose of meat production are called _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Broilers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Broilers** are domesticated **poultry birds** specifically bred and raised for **meat production**. They are known for their **fast growth rates** compared to birds kept for eggs. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• These birds are usually ready for **slaughter** at a very young **age**, typically between **6 to 8 weeks**, by which time they reach a weight of **1.5 to 2.5 kg**.
 
• The **nutritional requirements** for broilers are distinct, requiring **feed** that is rich in **proteins** and **fats** to support rapid **muscle development**.
 
• High levels of **Vitamin A** and **Vitamin K** are maintained in their **diet** to ensure healthy growth and prevent **deficiency diseases**.
 
• Common **examples** of broiler breeds include the **Cornish Cross**, **Plymouth Rock**, and **New Hampshire** chickens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Layers**: These are **poultry birds** raised primarily for the **production of eggs**. They reach **sexual maturity** and start **laying eggs** at the **age** of approximately **18 to 20 weeks**. Their **diet** requires a high amount of **calcium** and **phosphorus** to ensure the formation of strong **eggshells**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect for meat production.***
 
• **Cocks**: A **cock** or **rooster** is an **adult male chicken**. While they can be consumed for **meat**, in commercial **poultry farming**, they are predominantly used for **breeding** purposes to fertilize eggs. ***Hence, this option is incorrect as the primary term for meat-purpose birds.***
 
• **Fowls**: This is a general term that refers to **birds** belonging to the order **Galliformes**, such as **chickens**, **turkeys**, and **pheasants**. It is a broad category encompassing both **meat** and **egg-producing** birds rather than a specific commercial type. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Poultry Farming**: This **agribusiness** involves the **commercial rearing** of **domesticated birds**. It serves as a vital source of **animal protein** and contributes significantly to the **economy** of countries like **India**, **USA**, and **China**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Management Practices**: Broilers require specialized **housing management**. During the **brooding stage** (the first **14 days**), the **temperature** must be strictly controlled between **33°C to 35°C** for the **chicks** to survive.
 
• **Health and Hygiene**: Broiler flocks are susceptible to **diseases** such as **Ranikhet (Newcastle Disease)**, **Coccidiosis**, and **Bird Flu**. Regular **vaccination** and **sanitation** of the **poultry farm** are mandatory to prevent **mass mortality**.
 
• **Economic Data**: In **India**, the **poultry sector** is one of the **fastest-growing** segments of the **agricultural sector**, with a **growth rate** of nearly **8% to 10%** per **year**.
 
• **Feeding Efficiency**: Modern **broilers** have a **Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR)** of approximately **1.5 to 1.9**, meaning they convert **1.5 kg of feed** into roughly **1 kg of body weight**.
